lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: keeping personal health records privately

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic keeping personal health records privately task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Working only with an empty structural template (no real entries), the learner decides what categories a personal health record should include, describes where such a record could be kept securely, and sets a rule for who could view it, without recording any of the learner's own real health information anywhere in the template.
safetyNotes: This lesson produces an empty structural template only; no real health information, condition, or provider name is entered anywhere in the deliverable.
If the learner already keeps real records somewhere, they should not copy or reference any of that real content into this assignment.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Now that the template exists (empty), what would be different the next time you actually needed to look something up or tell a professional your history?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Category structure and coverage: Categories are distinct and cover the record types most people would need to track. | Storage-location reasoning: Location is named with a specific reason it is both reachable and appropriately private. | Access-rule specificity: Access rule names a specific person or role and a specific circumstance for sharing it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a fifth category for tracking questions that come up between visits so nothing is forgotten by the next appointment, and write one example of the kind of note that would go there.

resources.title: keeping personal health records privately coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Working only with an empty structural template (no real entries), the learner decides what categories a personal health record should include, describes where such a record could be kept securely, and sets a rule for who could view it, without recording any of the learner's own real health information anywhere in the template.
Coach direction: Before designing the template, think about what tends to go wrong when personal records are scattered or hard to find.
Learner prompt: Describe a time (yours or someone else's) when not having information organized and easy to find caused a problem -- in any area of life, not necessarily health.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: keeping personal health records privately complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Draft the category list your template would use to organize personal health records.

Response 1 (t2-p1): List the categories your health record template would include (for example: upcoming appointments, past visits, ongoing prevention reminders, questions to ask next time). Category names only -- do not fill in any real entries.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My category list contains no real health information, condition names, medications, or provider names -- only the names of the categories themselves.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: keeping personal health records privately minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Now that the template exists (empty), what would be different the next time you actually needed to look something up or tell a professional your history?

Success checks: Category structure and coverage: Categories are distinct and cover the record types most people would need to track. | Storage-location reasoning: Location is named with a specific reason it is both reachable and appropriately private. | Access-rule specificity: Access rule names a specific person or role and a specific circumstance for sharing it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: keeping personal health records privately supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional keeping personal health records privately condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Category structure and coverage: Categories are distinct and cover the record types most people would need to track. | Storage-location reasoning: Location is named with a specific reason it is both reachable and appropriately private. | Access-rule specificity: Access rule names a specific person or role and a specific circumstance for sharing it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
